settings.heading: Agents, sound and the art of exchange
settings.lede: A design and engineering case study for a cookware house that people can understand and machines can read. These are proposed experiences, not live shopping features.

settings.heading: The Kansa Bell Resonance Ritual
settings.text:
An opening acoustic and visual study would use the Web Audio API to model the harmonic decay of high-tin bell bronze: 22% tin and 78% copper. Each fading overtone would cue a restrained typography reveal. Sound would begin only after a visitor chooses it, with a silent and reduced-motion path.

This is a proposed ritual. The current storefront sound control is a separate opt-in interaction; it is not a measured simulation of this alloy.

settings.heading: Mol-Bhav: an algorithmic bazaar
settings.text:
Mol-bhav is mutual negotiation, rooted in a relationship of respect between patron and maker. The proposed arena lets a visitor start a bounded exchange between a buyer agent and Kansa, then watch a deterministic rule engine evaluate inventory age, bundle terms and a first-sale-of-the-day bohni rule.

A proposal token would identify an expiring offer for server-side verification. A later authenticated endpoint could display redacted packets from an outside agent or LLM. No visitor-facing offer, outside-agent connection or cryptographic token is live on this page.

settings.heading: A legible prototype, with clear limits
settings.text:
The current UCP room shows a labeled Mol-Bhav simulation, while Kansa answers prepared cookware questions. Neither is a live negotiation service. Product prices, stock and checkout remain with Shopify; any future proposal would be rechecked before purchase.

For the house and its craft context, read About Maison Tavo. For shopping questions, visit the FAQ.
